title: Super El Niño! Why Is Singapore So Hot And Dry? | TheOneApp, Explored EP13
desc:
In November 2026, the end of the year, Singapore still felt like an oven. Why? Shrink down with Pip, Momo and Basil and BE a gust of the trade wind over the Pacific Ocean: push the warm water west, watch it evaporate and condense into rain clouds, then grow weaker and watch the warm water and the rain clouds slide away east. That is El Niño. Find out what makes this one a Super El Niño, name the water cycle (evaporation and condensation), see how a drier year made the haze worse here in Singapore, and what El Niño is doing to the weather in India and the USA. Then be a weather detective with two cups of water.
